lines.text: HONG KONG, THE DOOR LEFT AJAR

lines.para: 1841. At the end of the First Opium War, the British take a nearly deserted rock at the mouth of the Pearl River. Kowloon follows in 1860; the New Territories are leased for ninety-nine years in 1898.

The colony becomes a free port where everything is traded: tea, opium, weapons, currency. It is also a refuge. Revolutionaries, losers of the civil war, exiles of every cause find shelter there, sometimes for a few months, sometimes for good.
For the secret services, it is a window onto China. People listen, recruit and trade there. British, Americans, Soviets, Chinese Nationalists and Communists drink in the same bars.
On 1 July 1997, Hong Kong returns to China under the formula “one country, two systems”. The door stays ajar. The question is which way it opens.
